Backed by a $25 million gift from the Charles Stewart Mott Foundation, MSU offers large or fully guaranteed salary coverage for researchers relocating substantial external funding portfolios. Highly accomplished senior faculty may also qualify for the C. S. Mott Endowed Professor of Public Health named professorship. About the Department and Community Founded in 2011 through a unique proposal from Flint-area hospitals and community members, the department operates on an unprecedented community-partnered model. As the first academic department to be co-developed and co-governed in partnership with the communities it serves, local citizens actively shape governance, focus areas, and serve on faculty hiring committees. Flint is a historic hub for community-based participatory research. This community-partnered approach has driven the Department’s external funding (over $500M since beginning in 2015) and real-world impact. Featured current projects include two NIH-funded Centers (focused on maternal health equity and suicide prevention) and Rx Kids, the nation’s first universal cash prescription program for infants and expectant mothers. Multiple Research-Intensive Associate/Full Professor Tenure System Positions MSU is seeking exceptional mid- to advanced-career investigators with innovative research portfolios and a history of external funding to join our energetic, mission-driven Department. Positions are 80-90% research effort. Public health issues of high importance originally identified by the Flint community include health equity; social determinants of health (violence, safety, the built environment, education, employment); behavioral health (mental health and substance use); healthy behaviors (including screening/prevention); and chronic disease. Recent events have also highlighted maternal and child health and environmental justice. Primary research methodologies are action-oriented: implementation science (including sustainment), dissemination and communication, intervention and services research, and research to change health policy. The post holders will spearhead projects in large-scale cancer genomics and evolution. The Cancer Genomics and Evolution laboratory Our research focuses on large-scale pan-cancer genomics to gain insight into the genes, mutational processes and evolution of cancer. Our work is highly data-driven, with a focus on large-scale data analysis to gain broad biological insight and on the development of computational methods to enable conceptually novel analyses. The research group is mostly computational with a small wet-lab component. Since its inception, members of the Cancer Genomics and Evolution laboratory have co-authored 22 papers in Nature, Cell or Science. Recent successes include studies of intra-tumor heterogeneity across cancers (Dentro et al., Cell 2021), the evolutionary history of cancer (Gerstung et al., Nature 2020), biallelic mutations in cancer genomes (Demeulemeester et al., Nature Genetics 2022), combined DNA methylation and genomic alterations in lung cancer evolution (Gimeno-Valiente et al., Nature Genetics 2025), benchmarking methods for subclonal reconstruction (Salcedo et al., Nature Biotechnology 2025), and the history of chromosomal instability in genome doubled tumors (Baker et al., Cancer Discovery 2024). Position qualifications The ideal candidate will have a PhD in computational biology (bioinformatics, genomics, …) and research experience in the field of cancer genomics, although we welcome applications from candidates with diverse educational backgrounds, including computational biology, physics and (bio)statistics, biology or medicine. Applicants must have a proven publication record. Prior experience with handling massively parallel sequencing data is considered an advantage. Postdocs will spearhead projects in cancer genomics and tumor evolution. They are expected to lead their own project, contribute to other projects on a collaborative basis (both within the lab and with external collaborators) and guide PhD students in their research. The ability to work in a team is essential. More information https://www.mdanderson.org/research/departments-labs-institutes/labs/van-loo-laboratory.html How to apply Please email pvanloo@mdanderson.org (1) a cover letter stating your general career objectives and research interests, (2) a CV with publication list, and (3) a list of three references. The successful candidate will be expected to establish a vibrant, externally funded research program, effectively teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students, and contribute to service in support of the department and college. We especially encourage applications from individuals who will complement existing departmental strengths in organismic evolutionary biology. The Biology Department provides a collaborative and broad research environment, with faculty whose research spans all levels of biological organization. This position will join a cohort of recent departmental hires in developmental cell biology, plant biology, neurobiology, and genetics. Faculty members in the biology department train graduate students through one or more interdepartmental graduate programs in Organismic and Evolutionary Biology, Molecular and Cellular Biology, Plant Biology, and Neuroscience and Behavior. Significant recent investments from these clinical partnerships, the State of Florida, and transformative philanthropy are converging to usher in a new era of biomedical research at Florida International University (FIU), creating an exceptional opportunity for faculty to establish ambitious collaborative research programs within a rapidly expanding academic medical center. HWCOM invites applications for full-time, tenure or tenure-track faculty positions at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor within the Department of Cellular & Molecular Medicine. As an academic and clinical affiliate of Baptist Health and Nicklaus Children’s Hospital, the HWCOM offers a unique environment for innovation and growth. The Department of Cellular & Molecular Medicine offers access to established core facilities including advanced bioimaging, flow cytometry, mass spectrometry, and mitochondrial bioenergetics; an interdisciplinary cohort of institutional faculty and facilities; a collaborative scientific community anchored by the Department's graduate program in Biomedical Science; modern research space within FIU's newly constructed biomedical research campus; and highly competitive start-up and recruitment packages. A strong background in general physiology is required; however preference will be given to applicants with experience teaching human renal and/or respiratory physiology. The physiology faculty team-teach in both discipline-specific and integrated basic science courses that serve students pursuing master’s degrees in biomedical sciences, and professional degrees in Osteopathic Medicine, Dental Medicine, Pharmacy, Optometry, Physical Therapy, Physician Assistant, and other professional healthcare programs. Faculty members are eligible for joint appointments in additional colleges based on research or teaching collaborations. Candidates are expected to establish an independent biomedical research program with the potential to attract extramural funding. The area of research is flexible, and both internal and external collaborative opportunities are strongly encouraged. Support for research activities includes access to a newly developed core equipment facility with strengths in histology, confocal imaging, and molecular and analytical biology. The MWU Animal Resource Facility is AAALAC accredited, and the institution holds NIH R15 (REAP) eligibility status. Dedicated laboratory space and start-up funds are provided to support the candidate’s research endeavors. Applications review will begin on September 1st, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. If you would like to learn more about this position, please submit your application through Midwestern University’s online job board at https://www.midwestern.edu/employment-mwu. Application packet must include: - A cover letter summarizing your interest in and suitability for a faculty position at MWU. - Curriculum Vitae, including your formal teaching experience, if any. - Personal statements of Teaching Philosophy, and Research Interests and Goals. - Contact information for a minimum of three references. The University has two campuses, one in Downers Grove, Illinois and the other in Glendale, Arizona. More than 6,000 full-time students are enrolled in graduate programs in osteopathic medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, physician assistant studies, physical therapy, occupational therapy, nurse anesthesia, cardiovascular perfusion, podiatry, optometry, clinical psychology, speech language pathology, biomedical sciences and veterinary medicine. We offer a work life balance with competitive time off package including paid holiday’s, sick/flex days, personal days and vacation days. We offer a 403(b) retirement plan, tuition reimbursement, child care subsidy reimbursement program, identity theft protection and an employee assistance program.
